subject.title: feat(sandbox): add sbx as a sandbox backend alongside OpenShell

question: Should OpenClaw sponsor and publish `@openclaw/sbx-sandbox` as an official optional sandbox plugin, including the new `sbx` backend selection and plugin configuration surface?
rationale: The implementation uses the intended external-plugin architecture, but selecting an additional officially supported sandbox runtime determines support burden, security posture, documentation, release ownership, and whether the dependency graph should be accepted.

options.title: Sponsor the official plugin
options.body: Accept `sbx` as an official optional sandbox backend, obtain security authorization for the reviewed dependency graph, and complete normal merge validation.

options.title: Route it to community ownership
options.body: Keep the public sandbox SDK seam unchanged and ask for an independently published community plugin without official-catalog and core-documentation inclusion.

options.title: Pause the integration
options.body: Defer this backend until an owner confirms demand, support expectations, and Docker Sandboxes security requirements.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the official plugin
recommendation.body: Accept `sbx` as an official optional sandbox backend, obtain security authorization for the reviewed dependency graph, and complete normal merge validation.

likelyOwner.reason: This is the closest identified current sandbox-backend contributor; security authorization should additionally route through `openclaw/openclaw-secops`.
